title: Rabbi Chiyya bar Avuyah
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: He was the grandfather of Rabbi Perida, as in Sanhedrin 82a: “Rabbi Chiyya bar Avuyah said: Whoever has relations with a Samaritan woman is as though he intermarries with idolaters.” And Rabbi Chiyya bar Avuyah said: “On the skull of Jehoiakim was written: This and yet another.” Rabbi Perida’s grandfather (he is Rabbi Chiyya bar Avuyah, according to Rashi) found a skull lying at the gates of Jerusalem, on which was written “This and yet another.” He buried it, and it emerged again … he said, “This is the skull of Jehoiakim … he is a king,” took it, wrapped it in silks and placed it in a chest. His wife found it; when she saw the head she told her neighbor, who said to her, “Certainly it is the head of his first wife, whom he cannot forget.” She took the head and burned it. When he came he said: “This is what is written on it: This and yet another.” Hyman therefore places him still in the days of the Tannaim, for Rabbi Perida, his grandson, lived in Rabbi’s days, as explained in his entry.

notes.text: The skull narrative is Hyman’s abridgment. ב״ב is understood as grandson, and the placement in the Tannaitic period remains Hyman’s inference; no new lineage is admitted.

The consulted Rashi on Sanhedrin 82a explicitly identifies Perida’s grandfather as Chiyya bar Avuyah. This is Rashi’s identification, not a new authority merge. The consulted Gemara reads a gentile woman, where Hyman supplies a Samaritan woman; Hyman’s abridged skull narrative and chronological argument remain his.
